name: G9/CT9 480-hour cybersecurity and AI-security program
provenance_note: Built in the repository from the Appendix A skeleton (seed 0.1.0-seed): every Appendix A objective keeps its wording as the start of its text and gains an observable success criterion; each objective is linked to the competencies it builds; each day gains hand-in criteria, versioned resources and a lesson (docs/curriculum/weeks/). Not reconciled and not approved: PROPOSED until the operator promotes it.

weeks.title: Linux, Python and secure lab engineering

objectives.text: Define lab authorization and boundaries — write a one-page scope statement: owner, permitted systems and actions, forbidden targets, data rules, time window and stop condition

Map host/guest and evidence isolation — draw the host, guest, network and evidence-store boundaries and prove with commands that a guest cannot reach the internet, the host's services or the evidence store
Establish diagnostic baseline — record the clean state of the lab (snapshot ids, listening ports, running services, hashes of key files) and score yourself on the week's diagnostic

days.evidence_artifact: Lab design + baseline — a dated scope statement, a boundary diagram with the isolation proof, and the recorded clean state of the lab (snapshot ids, listening ports, services, file hashes) with your first diagnostic scores.

objectives.text: Map OSI/TCP-IP layers — for one exchange between two lab guests name each layer's unit of data, address and protocol, and capture one packet that shows the headers of every layer
Explain addressing and subnetting — given a prefix compute network, broadcast, mask, usable range and host count by hand, verify with a tool, and say why two hosts are or are not on-link

days.evidence_artifact: Network architecture map — the addressing plan of the lab with the subnet arithmetic shown, the path of one request through every layer and hop, and the capture that proves each claim.

objectives.text: Assess business logic invariants — list the invariants of a small shop workflow (a balance never below zero, a coupon used once, stock never negative, only legal state transitions) and find where the code relies on the client or on call order to keep them

Examine controlled concurrency issue — reproduce a race (double redemption of a coupon, overdrawing a balance) with parallel requests against your application and show the interleaving that breaks the invariant

days.evidence_artifact: Business-logic report — the invariants of the workflow, the failures found, the concurrency demonstration and the fix with a repeatable regression test.

objectives.text: Trace model/dependency provenance — for each model, dataset, package and container image in the lab record where it came from, who published it, which version, which hash and under which licence

Assess licensing/integrity — check integrity (hashes, signatures, file format risks) and licence terms (including use restrictions of open-weight models) for each, and record what you could not verify

Define acquisition controls — define and implement controls for bringing new models and packages into the lab: allow-listed sources, hash pinning, scanning, quarantine, licence review and an approval record

days.evidence_artifact: Supply-chain review — the provenance record for each model and dependency of the lab, the integrity and licence assessment, a demonstration of a loading risk in the sandbox, and the acquisition controls with their tests.

objectives.text: Evaluate data poisoning — poison the training data of your small classifier in two ways (flipped labels, a trigger pattern) and measure the effect on accuracy and on triggered inputs, and test detection by data validation
Assess privacy exposure — show membership inference on an overfitted model, scan your corpus and logs for personal data, and list the places where data about a person persists
Define governance controls — specify and implement controls for data collection, provenance, access, retention and deletion, with checks that fail when a control is missing

days.evidence_artifact: Data security report — poisoning and privacy demonstrations on a small model in the lab, the data inventory with its lawful-use and retention decisions, and the governance controls with the checks that prove them.

objectives.text: Define valid metrics — for a stated claim choose metrics that measure it, say what each does not measure, and fix scoring rules, sample sizes and the analysis before running
Detect benchmark leakage — test whether evaluation items appear in training, tuning or retrieval data (exact and near matches, canaries) and measure the effect on the score
Create regression criteria — define thresholds that use intervals, a held-out set that stays held out, and a gate that blocks a change when a measure worsens beyond its interval

days.evidence_artifact: Evaluation protocol — the metrics and why they are valid for the claim, the leakage checks and their results, and the regression criteria with the gate that enforces them.

objectives.text: Assess unfamiliar AI scenario — build a threat model of an unseen AI system from its description and artefacts and run the bounded tests it allows
Produce evidence-linked findings — link every finding to an artefact, a test or a measurement, with uncertainty, and separate what you measured from what you assume
Verify control/limits — recommend and verify controls for the supply chain and data findings, and state the limits of every conclusion

days.evidence_artifact: Week 11 assessment — the report of the blind practical: the threat model of an unfamiliar AI system, the bounded tests with their results and uncertainty, the supply-chain and data findings, and the controls with the evidence and limits.

objectives.text: Define scope and authorization — write the scope statement and rules of engagement for the estate: owner, systems and addresses in scope, permitted and forbidden actions, rate, window, data handling, escalation and stop condition, with the authorization of the owner recorded

Build integrated threat model — draw the estate as one system (zones, hosts, identities, applications, data stores, pipelines, AI components) and derive the threats that cross layers, ranked with reasons

Establish acceptance rules — define the severity rubric, the evidence standard, the coverage required of each layer, the reproducibility rule and the completion criteria of the assessment before starting it

days.evidence_artifact: Capstone charter — the scope and rules of engagement for the estate, the integrated threat model across layers, the acceptance rules that say when the assessment is complete and how findings are rated and evidenced, and the baseline of the estate before assessment.

objectives.text: Assess isolated network — map the estate's zones and test its segmentation and name resolution against its intended policy within scope, interpreting discovery results with confidence

Evaluate controlled app weaknesses — test the web application and API for access control, token, request-forgery, upload and logic weaknesses, with two tenants and several roles, and prove each finding safely
Document remediation — for each finding write the root cause, the smallest remediation and a regression test, and apply and verify the ones within your remit

days.evidence_artifact: Network/app assessment — the findings for the network and for the web application and API, each with evidence, severity, root cause and remediation, and the verification that each remediation works.

objectives.text: Assess host/identity boundaries — enumerate the Linux and Windows hosts and the domain as a low-privilege principal and find the privilege paths and the trust problems
Explain access chain — explain the chain from the application foothold of the previous day to host and domain privilege as one path, with the right, trust or misconfiguration behind each step
Verify controls — cut the chain at its cheapest points, re-enumerate to show the chain is gone, and confirm the hardening baseline holds on every host in the chain

days.evidence_artifact: Host/identity assessment — the privilege paths on the hosts and in the domain, the access chain from an ordinary account to the surrogate privileged group, the controls that cut it and the proof that they hold.

objectives.text: Build telemetry/detection — build detections for the steps of the chains you found, with fixtures, conversions and a false-positive estimate against the estate's baseline
Investigate incident scenario — investigate the benign incident planted in the estate's telemetry from a stated hypothesis, correlating host, network and identity evidence into a labelled timeline
Demonstrate IR reasoning — scope and rate the incident, choose and justify containment, eradication and recovery steps with their risks, and state what you could not determine

days.evidence_artifact: Detection+IR package — the detections you built for the chains with their tests and false-positive estimates, the investigation of the incident in the telemetry with its timeline, and the incident response reasoning with scoping, severity and recovery recommendation.

objectives.text: Assess an AI/agent workflow — map the assistant's retrieval, the agent's loop, tools and the MCP server, with identities and authority crossings, and connect them to the chains of the estate

Test authorized trust boundaries — test, with harmless goals, the retrieval permissions, the tools' authority, the token handling of the MCP server and the injection paths, within the authorization of the charter

Verify mitigations — apply and verify the structural mitigations (typed enforcement, delegated authority, memory write controls) with deterministic tests and a pre-registered measurement for the model-dependent ones

days.evidence_artifact: AI security assessment — the map of the assistant, agent and MCP server in the estate, the findings on authorization and trust boundaries with harmless reproductions, the mitigations with deterministic tests, and the measured rates where the model matters.
